outcome: OASI severity (high-grade OASI vs. low-grade OASI)
cohort: The study population included women aged 18-50 years who underwent a vaginal delivery and were diagnosed with Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury (OASI).
finding: Operative vaginal delivery and higher parity are factors associated with more severe OASI, while artificial rupture of membranes was related to lower tear severity.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal delivery was associated with an increased risk of high-grade OASI.
